triples.subject: KGGen
triples.object: uses language models to extract high-quality graphs from plain text
triples.evidence: We present KGGen, a novel text-to-knowledge-graph generator that uses language models to extract high-quality graphs from plain text with a novel entity resolution approach that clusters related entities, significantly reducing the sparsity problem that plagues existing extractors.

triples.subject: KGGen
triples.object: to reduce sparsity in extracted KGs
triples.evidence: Unlike other KG generators, KGGen clusters and de-duplicates related entities to reduce sparsity in extracted KGs.

triples.subject: MINE
triples.relation: benchmark to test an extractor’s ability to produce a useful KG from plain text
triples.object: the first benchmark to test an extractor’s ability to produce a useful KG from plain text
triples.evidence: Along with KGGen, we release Measure of Information in Nodes and Edges (MINE), the first benchmark to test an extractor’s ability to produce a useful KG from plain text.

triples.evidence: We benchmark our new tool against leading existing generators such as Microsoft’s GraphRAG; we achieve comparable retrieval accuracy on the generated graphs and better information retention.

triples.subject: concise and generalizable entities and relations
triples.object: our graphs exhibit more concise and generalizable entities and relations
triples.evidence: Moreover, our graphs exhibit more concise and generalizable entities and relations.

triples.subject: Inductive knowledge graph completion
triples.object: predicting missing triplets between new entities
triples.evidence: Inductive knowledge graph completion has been considered as the task of predicting missing triplets between new entities that are not observed during training.

triples.subject: inductive knowledge graph completion methods
triples.relation: assume that all entities can be new
triples.object: they do not allow new relations to appear at inference time
triples.evidence: While most inductive knowledge graph completion methods assume that all entities can be new, they do not allow new relations to appear at inference time.

triples.subject: real-world knowledge graphs
triples.evidence: This restriction prohibits the existing methods from appropriately handling real-world knowledge graphs where new entities accompany new relations.

triples.subject: InGram
triples.relation: proposes an INductive knowledge GRAph eMbedding method
triples.object: that can generate embeddings of new relations as well as new entities at inference time
triples.evidence: InGram proposes an INductive knowledge GRAph eMbedding method, InGram, that can generate embeddings of new relations as well as new entities at inference time.

triples.subject: relation graph
triples.relation: consists of relations and the affinity weights between them
triples.object: based on the relation graph and the original knowledge graph
triples.evidence: Given a knowledge graph, we define a relation graph as a weighted graph consisting of relations and the affinity weights between them. Based on the relation graph and the original knowledge graph, InGram learns how to aggregate neighboring embeddings to generate relation and entity embeddings using an attention mechanism.

triples.subject: attention mechanism
triples.relation: used to learn how to aggregate neighboring embeddings
triples.object: to generate relation and entity embeddings
triples.evidence: Based on the relation graph and the original knowledge graph, InGram learns how to aggregate neighboring embeddings to generate relation and entity embeddings using an attention mechanism.

triples.subject: state-of-the-art methods
triples.object: state-of-the-art methods on varied inductive learning scenarios
triples.evidence: Experimental results show that InGram outperforms 14 different state-of-the-art methods on varied inductive learning scenarios.

triples.subject: A*Net

triples.evidence: Inspired by the A* algorithm for shortest path problems, our A*Net learns a priority function to select important nodes and edges at each iteration, to reduce time and memory footprint for both training and inference.

triples.subject: A*Net

triples.subject: LLMs
triples.object: scenarios requiring deep and responsible reasoning
triples.evidence: Although large language models (LLMs) have achieved significant success in various tasks, they often struggle with hallucination problems, especially in scenarios requiring deep and responsible reasoning.

triples.subject: external knowledge graphs (KG)
triples.evidence: These issues could be partially addressed by introducing external knowledge graphs (KG) in LLM reasoning.

triples.subject: Think-on-Graph (ToG)
triples.evidence: In this paper, we propose a new LLM-KG integrating paradigm ``$\hbox{LLM}\otimes\hbox{KG}$'' which treats the LLM as an agent to interactively explore related entities and relations on KGs and perform reasoning based on the retrieved knowledge.

triples.subject: LLM-KG integrating paradigm
triples.evidence: We further implement this paradigm by introducing a new approach called Think-on-Graph (ToG), in which the LLM agent iteratively executes beam search on KG, discovers the most promising reasoning paths, and returns the most likely reasoning results.

triples.subject: knowledge traceability
triples.relation: leveraging LLMs reasoning and expert feedback
triples.evidence: ToG has the ability of knowledge traceability and knowledge correctability by leveraging LLMs reasoning and expert feedback.

triples.subject: flexible plug-and-play framework
triples.relation: for different LLMs, KGs, and prompting strategies
triples.evidence: ToG provides a flexible plug-and-play framework for different LLMs, KGs and prompting strategies without any additional training cost.

triples.subject: LLM models
triples.evidence: the performance of ToG with small LLM models could exceed large LLM such as GPT-4 in certain scenarios and this reduces the cost of LLM deployment and application.

triples.subject: datasets
triples.evidence: As a training-free method with lower computational cost and better generality, ToG achieves overall SOTA in 6 out of 9 datasets where most previous SOTAs rely on additional training.

triples.subject: BioBridge
triples.evidence: BioBridge achieves it by utilizing Knowledge Graphs (KG) to learn transformations between one unimodal FM and another without fine-tuning any underlying unimodal FMs.

triples.subject: BioBridge
triples.evidence: Our results demonstrate that BioBridge can beat the best baseline KG embedding methods (on average by ~ 76.3%) in cross-modal retrieval tasks.

triples.subject: BioBridge
triples.evidence: We also identify BioBridge demonstrates out-of-domain generalization ability by extrapolating to unseen modalities or relations.

triples.subject: BioBridge
triples.evidence: Additionally, we also show that BioBridge presents itself as a general-purpose retriever that can aid biomedical multimodal question answering as well as enhance the guided generation of novel drugs.
